The instant writ petition has been filed for seeking directions to be used to the respondents to release a new commercial electricity connection with load of 48 KV in the premises of the petitioner with trade mark of "TANDOORI BITES" situated at Village Khajurala, Tehsil Phagwara, District Kapurthala.
texts.facts: 1. The instant writ petition has been filed for seeking directions to be used to the respondents to release a new commercial electricity connection with load of 48 KV in the premises of the petitioner with trade mark of "TANDOORI BITES" situated at Village Khajurala, Tehsil Phagwara, District Kapurthala. 2. Counsel for the petitioner contends that the petitioner is a partnership firm having its registered office at 2-A/124, Shankar Garden, Near Income Tax Colony, District Jalandhar and is running a Restaurant under the trade mark of "Tandoori Bites" situated at Village 1 of 33 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:082377 Khajurala, Tehsil Phagwara, District Kapurthala. He contends that the establishment started after executing a lease agreement dated 04.03.2003 with the then owner of the land. The Construction was thereafter, raised by the petitioner after spending huge amount and as per the terms and conditions of the lease agreement and for the purpose specified thereunder. With a gradual growth of business, more area of land was required and an additional fresh lease M/S K.B. Foods vs Punjab State Power Corporation Limited ... on 2 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65847261/ 1 agreement was executed on 11.08.2005. It is submitted that the petitioner continued to occupy the said premises and there has been no default in payment of any statutory dues and/or contractual obligations on the part of the petitioner. The original lessor namely, Naib Singh received entire lease money during his life time, however, he died in the year 2011 whereupon his estate was inherited by his widow, daughter and son and that they have been receiving the lease money in terms of the settlement as agreed between the parties. 3. Eventually, the LRs of Naib Singh sold the land to one Apinder Singh Nijjar vide sale deed dated 03.03.2020 whereupon, he became the lessor of the lease premises. The said lessor is a resident of U.S.A and one Kuljit Singh Bahia claims himself to be the attorney of said Apinder Singh Nijjar and it is contended that he started interfering in the lease premises of the petitioner, without any authority and legal justification and with a malicious intent to oust the petitioner. The said Civil Suit No. 20 of 2022 dated 18.10.2022 is pending before the Civil Judge (Junior Division), Phagwara. 5. Additionally, a Criminal Writ Petition No. 10255 of 2021 was also filed by the petitioner before this Court seeking protection of his life and liberty. The Inspector General of Police, Jalandhar Range was directed by this Court vide Order dated 28.10.2021 to look into the matter and to file his personal affidavit whereupon the affidavit was submitted. The said Criminal Writ Petition is stated to be still pending.
texts.arguments: 4. Aggrieved thereof, a suit was filed for declaration claiming that the petitioner is a lessee of the suit premises alongwith a prayer of an injunction to direct the respondents being successor-in-interest of suit 2 of 33 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:082377 property to get registered or execute registered lease deed/rent deed in favour of the petitioner with a further relief of a permanent injunction to restrain them from interfering the premises has also been sought. He contends that Kuljit Singh Bahia claiming himself to be the attorney of Apinder Singh Nijjar started interfering in the premises of which the petitioner is in an undisputed occupation with a mala fide intention and to forcibly grab the property by dispossessing the petitioner in an unlawful manner in connivance with the officials of the Punjab Police. He contends that the lessor, through his attorney, thereafter got the sanctioned load reduced from 90 KV to 1 KV which has caused severe prejudice to the petitioner in carrying out his day to day operations. 6. Considering that a higher load was required by it for operating the heavy electric/electronic equipments such as Deep Freezers, Refrigerators, Heavy Voltage Air Conditioners, Bear Making Machines as well as the necessary ventilation and lighting equipments, an application was thereafter, submitted by the petitioner for seeking release of a new 3 of 33 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:082377 commercial electricity connection with a load of 48 KV on 16.05.2024 and an application in this regard has been duly furnished. It is also submitted that the electricity Department had already appeared in the said Civil Suit and filed a written statement stating therein that the petitioner not being a Consumer as per their record, hence, he cannot seek change of the load on the pending electricity meter. Hence, the application seeking restoration of the earlier commercial electricity load was dismissed by Civil Judge (Junior Division), Jalandhar. The said order passed by the Civil Judge (Junior Division), Jalandhar has not been challenged by the M/S K.B. Foods vs Punjab State Power Corporation Limited ... on 2 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65847261/ 2 petitioner before any Court. Further, no separate application has been filed by the petitioner for seeking release of a fresh connection in the pending application. Instead, the petitioner submitted an application for new commercial electricity connection with the respondents but the same was allegedly not accepted by the official respondents by orally averring that a Court case is pending and as such they will not accept the application of the petitioner for release of a new commercial electricity connection. The said application was accordingly sent through a registered post on 03.06.2024 for issuance of a new commercial electricity connection. 7. The Counsel on behalf of petitioner has approached this Court by averring that in view of the judgment of this Court in the matter "Mobin Ansari versus Punjab State Power Corporation Limited and others" (2022(4) R.C.R (Civil) 782) as well as the subsequent judgment in the matter of "Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited versus Punjab State Power Corporation Limited and others"(2023(3) R.C.R (Civil)306, the 4 of 33 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:082377 petitioner is entitled to release of electricity connection since he is in an authorized and is in permissive possession of the premises in question under a valid lease agreement executed with him and that he cannot be dispossessed except a due process of law. The denial of the basic amenities to the petitioner cannot be permitted as a mode of seeking eviction of the petitioner from the premises in question as the same is likely to promote illegitimate means for seeking eviction of an occupant of the premises. 8. A specific question posed to the petitioner as regards the pendency of the Civil Suit and as to why the provisions of Order 2 Rule 2 of CPC would not be applicable especially when the suit was for permanent injunction to restrain the defendants/officials from disconnecting/changing the active load of the electricity connection bearing Account No. 3007557693 alongwith mandatory injunction for directing the restoration of the total electricity load was already pending and was subjudice. 9. Responding to the above, the Counsel for the petitioner submits that the suit was only for mandatory injunction and that the reduction in load was subsequent to the institution of the suit. 10. The said reply is erroneous on the facts of the case and is apparently an attempt to mislead this Court. The head note of the amended plaint appended by the petitioner alongwith instant writ petition as Annexure P-32 clearly shows that the suit was filed by the petitioner for permanent injunction to restrain the defendants, which includes the officials of the Punjab State Power Corporation Ltd. as well as the subsequent lessor from disconnecting/changing the active load of the electricity connection bearing 5 of 33 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:082377 Account No. 3007557693 and old meter connection No. 300607045. Thus, the cause of action for seeking relief against any change in the active load of the said electricity connection had already been invoked in the above said Civil Suit. Additionally, an application was also filed for seeking restoration of the said electricity connection and load which was dismissed by the Civil Court. The petitioner has a remedy available to him either to impugn the said order passed by the Civil Judge (Junior Division), Jalandhar before the Appellate Court or to move an appropriate application for an appropriate M/S K.B. Foods vs Punjab State Power Corporation Limited ... on 2 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65847261/ 3 interim relief of seeking release of a new electricity connection in view of the position in law relied upon by the petitioner and as laid down by this Court. The needful was however, not done and he instead is portraying the same as a new cause of action, despite an unsuccessful attempt of seeking restoration of the supply. Besides, the head note of the plaint clearly contemplates the change in the electricity connection as well as load and a restrain order was sought by the petitioner apart from a separate application seeking restoration. The claim having been already raised, failure on the part of the petitioner in securing the desired relief from Civil Court would not give a fresh cause of action to elect a different forum for the redressal of the same grievance for which he has failed to secure a favourable order in the suit before the Competent Court. 11.
